headline: Composio has no managed Xero app, but you can create your own Web app in minutes and connect up to 5 organisations free (50 on the AUD 35/month Core plan) with Composio's default scopes; going past 50 needs Xero certification, a bigger monthly fee and a yearly recertification.

notes: Standard authorization code flow for a 'Web app' that keeps a client secret. PKCE (S256 only) is for desktop and mobile apps; single-page apps are not supported.
No self-registration: Xero's OpenID discovery document has no registration_endpoint (tested 2026-10-20), so the app must be created by hand in My Apps.
Access tokens last 30 minutes. Refresh tokens expire if unused for 60 days and are replaced on every refresh. You only get one if you request offline_access.
Every organisation (tenant) a user ticks on the consent screen is a separate connection, and connections are what Xero's plans cap and charge for.
Redirect URIs must match exactly, use https (http://localhost is allowed for testing, 127.0.0.1 is not), cannot use wildcards, and you can save up to 50.
Since 2 March 2026, new apps can only request the new granular Accounting scopes. The old broad scopes (accounting.transactions, accounting.reports.read) are deprecated.

paths.label: Uncertified app, up to 50 connections (Starter, then Core)
paths.summary: Create a Web app yourself and go live with no review. The free Starter plan allows 5 connected organisations. Adding a credit card moves you to Core (AUD 35/month) for up to 50. Fits your own organisation, pilots and early customers.

badges.text: 5 connected organisations on the free Starter plan; up to 50 on Core. You are held at the cap until you meet the next plan's requirements.
Free for up to 5 connections. Connections 6 to 50 need the Core plan: AUD 35 a month plus tax, paid by credit card only.
Core includes 10 GB a month of data downloaded from Xero's APIs; more costs AUD 2.40 per GB. Starter has no egress charge.
Xero's developer terms require your app to have its own terms of use and privacy policy that users agree to.

start_here.action: Create a free Xero login, turn on the demo company, and create a Web app in My Apps with Composio's callback as the redirect URI.
Use Composio's default scope list as is. It is all granular scopes; do not add accounting.transactions or accounting.reports.read.
Add payment details in the developer portal to move from Starter to Core (up to 50 connections).

paths.label: Certified App Partner, up to 1,000 connections (Plus)
paths.summary: To pass 50 connections or list on the Xero App Store, apply for the Plus plan from Core. Xero reviews your integration against its certification checkpoints, then you pay AUD 245/month and recertify every year.

gates.title: Xero app certification (upgrade to Plus)
gates.trigger: You need more than 50 connected organisations, or a Xero App Store listing.
gates.avoid: Stay at or under 50 connections on Core (5 on the free Starter plan).

wait.note: Xero publishes no certification timeline. Codat, an integration vendor, reports that becoming a Xero App Partner can take several months.

gates.title: Annual recertification
gates.trigger: Every year after you are certified, to keep certification (and any App Store listing).

badges.text: Plus costs AUD 245 a month plus tax for up to 1,000 connections, with 50 GB of API egress included.
Egress above the monthly allowance costs AUD 2.40 per GB.
Certification makes you a Xero App Partner under the Developer Platform Commercial Terms. An App Store listing is optional at Plus.
Up to 1,000 connections, but held at 999 until you pass Xero's security self-assessment.
Your app needs its own terms of use and privacy policy.

start_here.action: Launch on Starter/Core and grow to ten active customer connections (real organisations, not the demo company).
Build the certification checkpoints: connect/disconnect settings page, error messages, launcher URL, offline_access.
In My Apps, open your app and click 'Manage Plan' to apply for Plus and certification.

paths.label: Over 1,000 connections or premium APIs (Advanced or Enterprise)
paths.summary: Above 1,000 connections, or to use the Journals endpoint, Practice Manager API or bulk connections, you need certification plus a security assessment that Xero repeats every year. Advanced is AUD 1,445/month; Enterprise is priced on application and needs an App Store listing.

gates.title: Xero app certification
gates.trigger: Required for every plan above Core.
gates.avoid: Stay at or under 50 connections on Core.

wait.note: Xero publishes no certification timeline. Codat, an integration vendor, reports that becoming a Xero App Partner can take several months.

gates.title: Security self-assessment reviewed by Xero
gates.trigger: Reaching 1,000 connections (Advanced plan), or using premium APIs such as Journals or Practice Manager.
gates.avoid: Stay under 1,000 connections on Plus and do not use the premium APIs.

wait.note: Xero's review time. Xero says filling in the assessment typically takes about 5 working days first. If items fail, you get 30 days to send a remediation plan and 60 days to make the changes.

gates.title: Use-case approval for premium APIs
gates.trigger: Only if you need the Journals endpoint (accounting.journals.read), the Practice Manager API or bulk connections.
gates.avoid: Use manual journals and reports instead of the Journals endpoint.

gates.title: Annual security assessment and recertification
gates.trigger: Every year after the first security assessment.

badges.text: Advanced costs AUD 1,445 a month plus tax for up to 10,000 connections; Enterprise (no limit) is priced on application.
Advanced includes 250 GB a month of API egress; more costs AUD 2.40 per GB.

Contact Xero developer support about use-case approval before you build on accounting.journals.read.

steps.title: Create a free Xero login
steps.detail: Sign up for a free Xero account. You use it to sign in to the Xero developer portal.

steps.title: Turn on the demo company for testing
steps.detail: In My Xero, enter the demo company. It is free and full of sample data. It resets 28 days after creation, and you must reconnect your app after each reset.

steps.title: Create a Web app in My Apps
steps.detail: Go to My Apps and click 'New app' (top right). Enter the App name (your product's name; it cannot contain the word Xero). Set Integration type to 'Web app' (the auth code flow). Enter your Company or application URL and the redirect URI below. Agree to the terms and click 'Create app'.

steps.title: Check the Composio redirect URI on the Configuration page
steps.detail: Open your app's Configuration page and make sure the URI below is saved exactly (https, no trailing slash). It must exactly match the redirect URI set in your Composio auth config. If you leave the auth config's redirect field at the Xero toolkit default, register the legacy https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add instead (or as well: Xero accepts up to 50 redirect URIs but no wildcards).

steps.title: Generate the client secret and copy both credentials
steps.detail: On the app page, click 'Generate a secret'. Copy the client ID and client secret and store them safely; after you save, the secret is hidden.

steps.title: Pick the scope list
steps.detail: Xero has no scope settings in the portal for Web apps; scopes are requested at connect time. Composio's defaults are all granular or unchanged scopes, so a new app can request them. Never add accounting.transactions, accounting.reports.read or accounting.journals.read to a new app. Add the optional extras only if you enable Composio's balance sheet or asset tools.

steps.title: Publish your terms of use and privacy policy
steps.detail: Xero's Developer Platform Terms require your app to have its own legally binding terms and privacy policy, and users must agree to them before using your app. Also note the terms ban using Xero API data to train or fine-tune AI models.

steps.title: Confirmed: no self-registration, PKCE S256
steps.detail: We fetched Xero's OpenID discovery document: there is no registration_endpoint (so no dynamic client registration), PKCE supports S256 only, and the grant types are authorization_code, client_credentials and refresh_token.

steps.title: Connect the demo company and run a read and a write
steps.detail: Connect through Composio and pick the demo company on Xero's consent screen. Every organisation a user ticks counts as one connection, so keep test connections few. Check the count in My Apps. If a user connects several organisations, pass tenant_id on every Composio tool call.

steps.title: Move to Core before your 6th connection
steps.detail: Starter stops at 5 connections. Add payment details (credit card) in the developer portal to move to Core: up to 50 connections, AUD 35 a month plus tax, 10 GB egress included. Billing is on the 1st of the following month.

steps.title: Reach ten active customer connections
steps.detail: Certification starts with a prerequisite check, including ten active customer connections. Use Core (up to 50) to onboard beta customers on real organisations.

steps.title: Build to Xero's certification checkpoints
steps.detail: Xero reviews: a settings page that shows the connected organisation and status, with connect and disconnect buttons (disconnect with DELETE on the Connections endpoint); handling disconnects made from Xero; a 'Login URL for launcher' in your app's Configuration; minimal scopes with offline_access; clear error messages; correct data, account mapping and tax. Our estimate of build time.

steps.title: Apply for Plus and certification from 'Manage Plan'
steps.detail: Log in to the developer portal, select your app and click 'Manage Plan' to upgrade from Core to Plus; certification is part of the upgrade. Xero checks prerequisites and reviews your integration, and may ask you to provision a test account for them. Answer reviewer questions promptly.

steps.title: Complete the security self-assessment
steps.detail: Xero sends the assessment at 800 connections or when you ask for premium API access. Allow about 5 working days to fill it in; Xero then takes 5 to 10 working days to assess it. Failed items need a remediation plan within 30 days and fixes within 60 days. It repeats every year.

while_you_wait.text: Build and test against the free demo company. It resets 28 days after creation, so reconnect after each reset.
Starter allows 5 connected organisations and 1,000 API calls per organisation per day (5,000 on Core and above). Use them for your own organisation, the demo company and first pilots.
Stay on Core (up to 50 connections) while certification is in progress; your beta customers there count toward the ten active connections Xero checks.
Watch your connection count in My Apps and disconnect inactive organisations: they still count toward your plan and your bill.

blockers.symptom: Xero shows 'Sorry, something went wrong' or an 'Invalid scope' error before the consent screen.
blockers.cause: A new app (created on or after 2 March 2026) asked for a retired broad scope (accounting.transactions, accounting.reports.read) or accounting.journals.read. The same screen appears when the redirect URI or client ID does not match.
blockers.fix_now: Use Composio's default scope list unchanged, remove any broad or journals scope, and check the redirect URI matches one saved in My Apps exactly.
blockers.fix_properly: Request only the granular scopes your enabled tools need. If you truly need the Journals endpoint, plan for the Advanced plan.

escalate.how: Xero Developer support form. Give the app name exactly as in My Apps.
escalate.draft: Our Web app "<app name>" (client ID <id>, created <date>) gets an 'Invalid scope' error at login.xero.com/identity/connect/authorize. Scopes requested: <list>. Which of these is not available to our app, and what should we request instead?

blockers.symptom: New customers cannot connect once you have 5 connected organisations (or 50 on Core).
blockers.cause: Each plan caps connections, and every organisation a user ticks counts, including the demo company and test organisations. You stay capped until you meet the next plan's requirements.
blockers.fix_now: Disconnect test and inactive organisations with 'manage your connections' in the developer portal (needs the Owner role), or add a credit card to move to Core.
blockers.fix_properly: Start certification well before you reach 50 connections; Xero publishes no timeline for it.

escalate.how: Xero Developer support form, to ask about moving plans.
escalate.draft: Our app "<app name>" is at <n> connections on the <Starter/Core> plan. We want to move to <Core/Plus>. What do we still need to complete, and how long does certification usually take?

blockers.symptom: A Composio Xero tool fails with HTTP 401 and a WWW-Authenticate insufficient_scope header (for example the balance sheet, fixed assets or journals tools).
blockers.cause: The connection's token lacks the scope that endpoint needs. Composio's default list leaves out accounting.reports.balancesheet.read and assets.read, and accounting.journals.read is only for the Advanced plan.
blockers.fix_now: Add the missing scope to your auth config and send the user through Connect again; Xero needs fresh consent for new scopes.
blockers.fix_properly: Before launch, map each Composio tool you enable to its Xero scope and request them all up front.

escalate.how: Xero Developer support form; include the X-Correlation-Id header from the failed response.
escalate.draft: Calls to <endpoint> return 401 insufficient_scope for tenant <tenant id>. Correlation ID: <id>. The token has scopes <list>. Which scope does this endpoint need?

blockers.symptom: The customer's organisation is missing from the drop-down on Xero's consent screen, or they cannot add your app.
blockers.cause: The user needs a Standard, Adviser or Administrator role with the Connected Apps permission, or the app is already connected to that organisation. Each organisation can also connect only a limited number of uncertified apps (Xero's docs say five; an older FAQ says two).
blockers.fix_now: Ask a user with the right role to connect. If the organisation is at its uncertified-app limit, the customer can disconnect an unused uncertified app.
blockers.fix_properly: Get certified: Xero sets no per-organisation limit on certified apps.

escalate.how: Xero Developer support form, with the organisation name as it appears in Xero.
escalate.draft: A customer (organisation "<org name>") cannot connect our app "<app name>". Their user has the <role> role. Is the organisation at its uncertified-app limit, or is something else blocking it?

blockers.symptom: A connection that worked stops: API calls return 403 AuthenticationUnsuccessful, or token refresh returns invalid_grant.
blockers.cause: The demo company reset (every 28 days), the user's role changed or access was revoked, or the refresh token went unused for 60 days.
blockers.fix_now: Send the user through Connect again to create a fresh connection.
blockers.fix_properly: Keep offline_access in your scopes, make at least one call per connection well within 60 days, and show a 'Reconnect to Xero' prompt when calls fail.

escalate.how: Xero Developer support form; include the X-Correlation-Id of a failed call.
escalate.draft: Tenant <tenant id> on our app "<app name>" returns 403 AuthenticationUnsuccessful since <date>. Correlation ID: <id>. The user has not disconnected the app. Can you see why the connection is no longer authorised?

unknowns.question: Does Xero expect certification before you offer an app to customers on Core (connections 6 to 50)?
unknowns.why: Xero's commercial terms and one FAQ answer say certification applies from Core, while the plan table, the limits page and the tier FAQ show Core needs only a payment method. If certification were enforced at Core, external use beyond 5 connections would need a review.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Ask Xero Developer support before onboarding your 6th customer, and check the requirements shown in 'Manage Plan'.

unknowns.question: How long does certification take?
unknowns.why: It decides when you can pass 50 connections. Xero publishes no timeline; Codat reports several months.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Ask your Xero developer contact when you apply via 'Manage Plan', or ask in Xero's developer office hours.

unknowns.question: What the annual recertification involves for a Plus app that is not listed on the App Store
unknowns.why: The commercial terms mention an annual recertification process but do not describe it; it adds recurring work.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Xero says it explains the requirements when you apply for certification; ask then.

unknowns.question: Is 'Sign Up with Xero' required for certification?
unknowns.why: The certification checkpoints say it is not required, but the partner guide lists it as a prerequisite and the pricing FAQ says App Store apps need it. It could add build work.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Confirm with Xero when you apply; plan to build it if you want an App Store listing.

unknowns.question: How many uncertified apps can one customer organisation connect: five or two?
unknowns.why: Customers who already use several uncertified apps may be unable to connect yours.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Ask Xero Developer support; the limits page (five) is the more recent of the two sources.

composio_notes.text: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Xero, so you must bring your own Xero app before any user can connect.

Redirect URI: register Composio's current callback, https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback, and make it match the redirect URI in your Composio auth config exactly. The Xero toolkit default still points at the legacy https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add; if you keep that default, register the legacy URI. Xero allows up to 50 redirect URIs, so registering both is harmless.

Composio's Xero setup guide still lists the broad scopes accounting.transactions and accounting.reports.read. Do not copy them: apps created on or after 2 March 2026 cannot request them. Composio's toolkit default scopes are already the granular ones.

Some Composio Xero tools need scopes outside the default list: the balance sheet tool needs accounting.reports.balancesheet.read, the asset tools need assets.read, and the List Journals tool needs accounting.journals.read, which only Advanced-plan apps get.
Composio's Xero tools take an optional tenant_id; if you leave it out they use the first connected organisation. Pass it explicitly when a user connects more than one organisation.

Xero's Custom Connections (client credentials, one organisation, paid monthly by that organisation) do not fit Composio's Xero toolkit, which uses the OAuth2 redirect flow. Use a Web app even for your own organisation.
For agent builders: Xero's developer terms ban using data from its APIs to train or fine-tune AI models, including LLMs. Keep Xero data out of any training or fine-tuning sets.
